chunks.title: About NEST · nest.curiosta.com
chunks.heading: How our domains map to official frameworks
chunks.text: NEST groups work into 22 physical-work domains in plain language. These are our own groups , not an official classification. India's official frameworks cut the same work differently: the National Qualification Register (NQR) lists qualifications and the body that awards each one, and each qualification file names the matching code in the National Classification of Occupations 2015 (NCO-2015). The table shows one example qualification per domain where we checked the NQR page and its qualification file on 19 Oct 2026. One domain can span several skill councils and many NCO codes, so read this as a pointer, not a full map.

chunks.title: About NEST · nest.curiosta.com
chunks.heading: How we verify fairs
chunks.text: NEST lists job fairs only — not individual vacancies. Every card must have an official URL we can check. Verification levels Gov — Listed on NCS, state employment / e-Rozgar, ministry, or PIB with a durable official page. NSDC — NSDC Rozgar Mela / JobX / SSC-announced programme pages. Campus — University, ITI, or polytechnic official placement notice. Industry — CII, FICCI, ASSOCHAM, or sector chamber official page. Private-verified — Named organiser + public registration page + evidence of recurrence (or a clear first-edition official page). Flyer-only fails. Date honesty Exact dates for upcoming editions only when officially announced.

chunks.title: About NEST · nest.curiosta.com
chunks.heading: How we verify fairs
chunks.text: Exact dates for past 2026 editions when backed by official pages and/or durable news corroboration (e.g. PIB, state portals, organiser site + PTI). Otherwise “Usually …” or “Not yet announced · Last: …” for recurring hubs. We never invent dates. Past cards show a Past badge when the start date is before today. Physical-domain rule Fairs need not be physical-only. Mixed multi-sector events are OK.

chunks.title: About NEST · nest.curiosta.com
chunks.heading: How we verify fairs
chunks.text: They must include physical-domain jobs (bedside, trades, floor, field, agri/food, hospitality/food service, emergency/safety, wet-lab, live-events hardware, energy & utilities field, care, repair & field maintenance, security/defence/policing, teaching & hands-on training, sports/fitness/wellness, mining/maritime/offshore, survey & geospatial field, animal care & veterinary, home/sanitation/waste services, craft & heritage trades, data centres & cooling, electronics/chips/robotics). Desk-only hiring events are out unless they hire for Human in the Loop roles, such as data annotation or AI review; those still need an official page.

chunks.title: About NEST · nest.curiosta.com
chunks.heading: How we verify fairs
chunks.text: Drop rules Flyer / WhatsApp-only with no official URL News article without an organiser page Desk-only hiring events with no Human in the Loop roles (software, pure remote knowledge work) Individual job listings (out of scope for this calendar) Propose a fair Send Manoj or Manasi (NEST's founders) the official page URL, city, dates, organiser type, and which physical domains it serves. Soft submissions without an official URL will be declined. See also calendar/sources.md .

chunks.title: About NEST · nest.curiosta.com
chunks.heading: What's out
chunks.text: NEST is opinionated. If an agent can finish the work at a desk with no human check, it does not belong on this site — even if a fair mentions it. Software engineering / “full stack” desk roles Pure data analysis / BI without field ops SEO, content mills, prompt-only “AI jobs” Prompt engineering and other laptop roles where no person checks or signs off the AI's output Remote-only tutoring / freelance writing Call-centre scripting without field service Desk-only design / PM with no physical build Generic “digital marketing” WFH listings Crypto / trading desk roles Borderline cases (e.g. field service with a digital ticket system) stay in when the core work is physical.

chunks.title: About NEST · nest.curiosta.com
chunks.heading: What's out
chunks.text: When unsure, we ask: would an agent at a laptop finish the job with no human check? Physical work that AI creates — data-centre power and cooling, robot and drone maintenance, field data collection — is in : see Work for AI . Human in the Loop roles are in , at a desk or in the field: data labelling and annotation, content moderation, AI output review, clinical and legal review of AI, fraud and claims review, robot teleoperation, drone piloting, autonomous-vehicle safety operation, on-site AI quality inspection and warehouse exception handling. The test: does a person supervise, correct, approve or take over from the AI? See Human in the Loop . See what's in

chunks.title: Job-fair calendar · NEST
chunks.heading: How we built this calendar
chunks.text: Levels it hires for: none of the fair sources in this calendar says which rung of the AI role ladder (L1 to L4) its roles need, so no fair carries a level tag; we do not guess. Go one level up: whatever job you find here, you can learn to direct AI agents with expert-written skills. See the AI role ladder . Fairs on record rows come from our own verified fairs since October 2021. Peak means we verified fairs in that month in two or more different years. Possible means at least one. National Rozgar Mela appointment-letter ceremonies are listed as fairs but not counted in the bands, because they are not open fairs.

chunks.title: Job-fair calendar · NEST
chunks.heading: How we built this calendar
chunks.text: Sourced rows are recruitment seasons that a cited source describes: festive-season hiring for logistics, Agniveer rally schedules, kharif and rabi crop seasons, and engineering campus placements. Where a source gives no month, we leave it blank. Blank always means no data.

chunks.title: Job-fair calendar · NEST
chunks.heading: How we built this calendar
chunks.text: Economic Times (29 Aug 2025): e-commerce platforms ramp up seasonal hiring ahead of festivities, 3.8 lakh jobs TeamLease (8 Sep 2025): festive hiring eases to 15-20% in 2025 but still adds 2.16 lakh jobs Indian Army zone-wise rally schedule, recruiting year 2025-26 (copy on studyandupdates.in) Indian Army Agniveer rally schedule 2025 (copy on testbook.com) Indian Economic Service, Arthapedia: cropping seasons of India (kharif and rabi) Mint (2 Oct 2025): India campus placements 2026, when institutes place Fairs show an exact date only when an official page or news report gives one.

chunks.title: Job-fair calendar · NEST
chunks.heading: How we built this calendar
chunks.text: Status (Upcoming, On now, Ended) is worked out in your browser from today's date, and fairs that are over move to “Already held”. Recurring fairs whose next dates are not announced yet sit under Coming up in their usual month where we know it, marked “Dates not announced yet”, with the last edition we verified. Organiser types: Gov · NSDC · Campus · Industry · Private-verified . Each fair shows its organiser type; read how we verify fairs . Every fair, season and dropped item is logged with its source in sources.md . Fairs checked 5–6 Oct 2026; new-domain fairs 11 Oct 2026; seasons checked 12 Oct 2026. Each domain page links straight to its fairs here.

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: Agri / food processing / cold chain
chunks.text: Primary production and wet processing happen in physical plants and fields. Agents may advise agronomy; harvesting, processing lines, and cold-store work stay embodied. Livestock, dairy, poultry and veterinary work has its own domain since 11 Oct 2026: Animal care & veterinary . Fairs tagged Agri / food processing / cold chain All domains

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: Start here
chunks.text: Voice advisers and drones reach farmers, but someone trained still has to fly, spray, process and check the food. Most people enter as farm worker with machinery training, plant helper. The routes below get you to L1; the ladder underneath shows how the work changes at each rung. NEST view L1 These routes prepare you for L1, Intelligent Proxy . The next rung, L2 Orchestrator , needs time on the job running a crew's work plus several AI tools. NEST view ITI trade ( DGT CTS list ): Horticulture , Agro Processing , Food Production (General) , Dairying . Apprenticeship : NAPS, through apprenticeshipindia.gov.in ( PIB ). Job fairs and career centres : National Career Service (NCS) .

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: Start here
chunks.text: Skill council course : Agriculture Skill Council of India (ASCI) and Food Industry Council for Skills and Innovation (FICSI) ; their qualification packs (QPs) are listed on the National Qualification Register (NQR) . Qualifications on the NQR for this work include Micro-Irrigation Technician (NSQF level 4); Assistant Technician – Cold Storage (NSQF level 3); Kisan Drone Operator (NSQF level 3). Check that a training centre is accredited for the exact qualification before you enrol. Verified fairs tagged to this domain: 9 . Typical progression on this page is labelled NEST view; we give no salaries.

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: Levels in this domain
chunks.text: L1 Intelligent Proxy Uses expert AI skills; does the physical work L2 Orchestrator Runs several AI tools and a crew's workflow L3 Skill developer Writes the skills others use L4 Harness and model builder Builds the tools skills run on Roles here are evolving along the AI role ladder . Most people start at L1, Intelligent Proxy: the trained person on site who uses expert-written AI skills and stays accountable for the physical work. Example roles at each rung .

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: Levels in this domain
chunks.text: NEST view L1 Intelligent Proxy Farmer using a scheme-application skill in a phone browser Example: farmers ask Kisan e-Mitra, a voice AI chatbot, in their own language (PIB) L2 Orchestrator FPO manager running agents for procurement, inputs and buyer follow-up Example: Amul's call centre, Pashu Seva app, ear-tag records and service ticketing run as one system L3 Skill developer Agronomist writing a pest-scouting and spray-safety skill NEST view L4 Harness and model builder Agri-tech engineer with agronomists, building and fine-tuning crop-advisory and crop-disease models for local crops and languages. Example: ITC's Krishi Mitra GenAI co-pilot (ITCMAARS)

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: What each rung looks like here
chunks.text: Composite sketches, not real people, grounded in the tools and employers on this page. NEST view L1 Intelligent Proxy: a day at this rung Farmer. This person loads a scheme-application skill and a voice farm adviser on the phone. On the job, this person still works the field, sprays and harvests. Where they stop and consult: pesticide doses and crop disease beyond the basics go to the agriculture officer or a Krishi Vigyan Kendra expert. The AI speeds up the routine part; the judgement and the accountability stay with the person. NEST view L2 Orchestrator: a day at this rung FPO manager. This person loads agents for procurement, inputs and buyer follow-up.

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: What each rung looks like here
chunks.text: On the job, this person still visits members' fields and checks produce at collection. Where they stop and consult: contract and payment disputes go to the FPO board. The AI speeds up the routine part; the judgement and the accountability stay with the person. NEST view L3 Skill developer: a day at this rung Agronomist. This person loads a pest-scouting and spray-safety skill. On the job, this person still scouts real fields with farmers to test it. Where they stop and consult: chemical advice is checked against official guidance before release. The AI speeds up the routine part; the judgement and the accountability stay with the person.

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: What each rung looks like here
chunks.text: NEST view L4 Harness and model builder: a day at this rung Agri-tech engineer. This person loads crop-advisory and crop-disease models for local crops and languages. On the job, this person still visits plots to collect and check ground truth. Where they stop and consult: advice is validated with agronomists before farmers see it. The AI speeds up the routine part; the judgement and the accountability stay with the person. NEST view

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: Demand signals
chunks.text: PIB: as of 30 Jun 2026, 1,735 PM Kisan SAMPADA projects approved and 1,256 completed, with processing capacity of 294.21 LMT a year and 9.16 lakh employment opportunities. Source: PIB (PRID 2291794): PM Kisan SAMPADA Yojana What we read in this: We read this as processing-plant, cold-store and drone roles absorbing new work; safe drone spraying and food-safety checks are the bottleneck skills. L1 is the most accessible rung in the next 12 to 18 months. NEST view

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: How roles and teams are shifting
chunks.text: Apps, sensors and tagged-animal records turn field visits into data-driven work. Field staff and paravets act as L1 proxies; experts who write the advisories move to L3. NEST view See the AI role ladder →

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: With AI / For AI
chunks.text: With AI Kisan e-Mitra, a voice AI chatbot, answers farmers in 11 languages; [13] Namo Drone Didi gives women SHGs spraying drones with pilot and drone-assistant training. [9] For AI AI crop data starts in the field: Digital Crop Survey surveyors must be at the plot, and the app uses geofencing and AI image checks. [14] [15] Paths: ITI Drone Technician; IoT Technician (Smart Agriculture). [18] More on Work with AI → Work for AI

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: Recording skills for robots
chunks.text: Farm and food-processing work is also being recorded first-person for robot training. Recorders are L1; annotators and reviewers L2; task designers L3; robot-model trainers L4. NEST view Graveiens AI records on farms The recording ladder · Before you record: consent, pay, data

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: ITC (Agri Business / ITCMAARS)
chunks.text: Large agri sourcing & foods player engaging farm + processing value chains How they run their tech Official ITCMAARS “phygital” ecosystem: farmer super-app, soil tests, remote sensing, IoT weather/moisture sensors, drone fertilisation services, market-price intelligence, and vernacular GenAI co-pilot (Krishi Mitra) — digital advisory layered on FPO field networks. Source: ITC — ITCMAARS NextGen Agriculture · checked 6 Oct 2026 What it changes Field extension staff shift from visiting every farm to acting on app, sensor and satellite alerts; farmer-facing staff work as L1 proxies with the co-pilot, while agronomists move up to writing the advisories (L3). NEST view

chunks.title: Agri / food processing / cold chain · NEST
chunks.heading: Amul Dairy (Kaira Union / GCMMF network)
chunks.text: Cooperative dairy system employing plant, cold-chain & field vet/collection roles How they run their tech Official digitalisation page: 24×7 Centralized Veterinary Call Center, Amul Pashu Seva app, animal ear-tagging integrated with treatment/AI software (~99% tagged in milk-shed), BMC/plant service ticketing, GPS vehicle tracking for vet vans, and SMS case workflows. Source: Amul Dairy — Digitalization of Veterinary Services · checked 6 Oct 2026 What it changes Village paravets and call-centre staff work from tagged-animal records and tickets, so dispatch and follow-up merge into one digital loop; supervisors orchestrate the queue (L2). NEST view

chunks.title: Animal care & veterinary · NEST
chunks.heading: Animal care & veterinary
chunks.text: Helping a cow calve, vaccinating a flock, treating an injured dog or rescuing a leopard from a well needs hands, calm and judgement. Herd apps and helplines route the call; a trained person examines the animal. Works hand in hand with Agri / food processing / cold chain : dairy, poultry and fisheries feed that domain's supply chains. Fairs tagged Animal care All domains

chunks.title: Animal care & veterinary · NEST
chunks.heading: Start here
chunks.text: Herd records and helplines plan the visit; handling and treating the animal stays hands-on. Most people enter as farm or shelter attendant, poultry helper, rescue volunteer. The routes below get you to L1; the ladder underneath shows how the work changes at each rung. NEST view L1 These routes prepare you for L1, Intelligent Proxy . The next rung, L2 Orchestrator , needs time on the job running a crew's work plus several AI tools. NEST view ITI trade ( DGT CTS list ): Dairying , Milk & Milk Product Technician . Apprenticeship : NAPS, through apprenticeshipindia.gov.in ( PIB ). Job fairs and career centres : National Career Service (NCS) .

Qualifications on the NQR for this work include Artificial Insemination Technician (NSQF level 4); Livestock Service Provider (NSQF level 4); Dairy Worker (NSQF level 2.5). chunks.title: Animal care & veterinary · NEST
chunks.heading: Demand signals
chunks.text: Lok Sabha answer (Jul 2026): 4,019 Mobile Veterinary Units operational in 29 States / UTs; farmers call the toll-free 1962 line and call centres with veterinarians dispatch a unit. Source: Lok Sabha (DAHD) NDDB Annual Report 2024-25: 1,683 Multi-Purpose AI Technicians (MAITRIs) deployed across the North-Eastern states performed over 46.62 lakh artificial inseminations. Source: NDDB What we read in this: We read this as para-vets, AI technicians and mobile-unit staff absorbing field work; safe animal handling is the bottleneck skill. L1 is the most accessible rung in the next 12 to 18 months. NEST view

chunks.heading: Care: elder, disability & child

Apps can remind and monitor; they cannot hold a hand or notice that a child is frightened. New on 11 Oct 2026: split out of the former “Hospitality & care frontline” domain, which is now Hospitality & food-service frontline . Fairs tagged Care All domains

chunks.title: Skilled construction & trades · NEST
chunks.heading: What each rung looks like here
chunks.text: Composite sketches, not real people, grounded in the tools and employers on this page. NEST view L1 Intelligent Proxy: a day at this rung Site supervisor. This person loads a daily safety-check skill on a phone. On the job, this person still walks the scaffolding, checks harnesses and stops unsafe work. Where they stop and consult: structural doubts go to the site engineer, and electrical faults to a licensed electrician. The AI speeds up the routine part; the judgement and the accountability stay with the person. NEST view L2 Orchestrator: a day at this rung Site engineer. This person loads agents for material take-offs, schedules and snag lists.

chunks.title: Skilled construction & trades · NEST
chunks.heading: What each rung looks like here
chunks.text: On the job, this person still inspects the work on site before approving any agent output. Where they stop and consult: design changes go to the structural consultant. The AI speeds up the routine part; the judgement and the accountability stay with the person. NEST view L3 Skill developer: a day at this rung Experienced engineer. This person loads a pour-readiness inspection skill drawn from years of site work. On the job, this person still checks shuttering and reinforcement in person when testing the skill. Where they stop and consult: the skill is signed off by the project's structural engineer. The AI speeds up the routine part; the judgement and the accountability stay with the person.

chunks.text: Weaving, pottery, carving and heritage restoration are valued because a skilled person makes them by hand. Design software can suggest a pattern; the loom, the wheel and the lime mortar still need the craftsperson. An honest note: most craft melas and trade fairs are sales events, where artisans sell to buyers. They are not hiring fairs. NEST lists only verified hiring fairs here, so this domain's calendar filter may show none. Much craft work is self-employed or runs through co-operatives and producer groups. chunks.heading: Data centres & cooling
chunks.text: Server halls run 24×7 on power, cooling and cables that people install, watch and repair on site. AI runs inside these buildings; it cannot change a UPS battery, fix a chiller leak or splice a fibre. Split out on 12 Oct 2026 from Energy & utilities field , Repair & field maintenance and Skilled construction & trades . Grid, substation and solar work stays under Energy; putting up the building stays under Construction. An honest note: no hiring fair aimed only at data-centre jobs was verified this pass, so the calendar filter shows the all-domain hubs. Fairs tagged Data centres All domains

chunks.title: Data centres & cooling · NEST
chunks.heading: Demand signals
chunks.text: Data-centre capacity in India grew from about 375 MW in 2020 to about 1,500 MW by 2025; the Ministry of Power estimates data-centre electricity demand at 13.56 GW by 2031-32. Source: PIB (13 Mar 2026): data-centre capacity and cooling, Rajya Sabha reply To cut water use, the industry is adopting direct-to-chip liquid cooling, adiabatic cooling and immersion cooling , and high-density racks for AI workloads. Source: PIB (13 Mar 2026): data-centre capacity and cooling, Rajya Sabha reply 1.6 GW operational in primary markets, 322.4 MW under construction and more than 8 GW committed and planned (2025).

chunks.title: Data centres & cooling · NEST
chunks.heading: Demand signals
chunks.text: Source: Knight Frank: India Data Centre Market Update 2025 The sector employs about 86,000-90,000 people; cooling and electrical facilities roles are projected to grow more than 100% through 2029. Source: Quess: India data-centre talent report What we read in this: We read capacity growth as demand for shift electricians, cooling and fibre technicians; liquid-cooling and high-density rack skills are becoming the bottleneck. L1 is the most accessible rung in the next 12 to 18 months. NEST view

chunks.title: Repair & field maintenance · NEST
chunks.heading: Urban Company
chunks.text: Home-services platform training AC, appliance, electrical and plumbing professionals How they run their tech Annual Report 2024-25: 220+ training rooms in 15 cities and 200+ permanent trainers (31 Mar 2025); a service-professional app that guides diagnosis and SOP adherence, uses image and barcode scans for proof-of-work, and vision-based ML to confirm a professional's identity before a job. Source: Urban Company Annual Report 2024-25 · checked 11 Oct 2026 What it changes A guiding app with image and barcode proof-of-work turns technicians into L1 proxies who follow expert SOPs; the 200+ permanent trainers who shape those SOPs sit higher on the ladder (L3). NEST view

chunks.title: Repair & field maintenance · NEST
chunks.heading: Blue Star
chunks.text: Air-conditioning and refrigeration maker with a national after-sales service network How they run their tech Investor presentation (Q4 FY24, BSE filing 3 May 2024): 2 million+ service calls a year; a remote-monitoring centre at Thane; a field-service technician app to update and close breakdown and maintenance tickets with all parameters recorded digitally; Star Vault knowledge-management system. Source: Blue Star investor presentation, May 2024 (BSE filing) · checked 11 Oct 2026 What it changes A remote-monitoring centre and a technician app put diagnosis and ticket closure into one system; field technicians act on remote insight, and dispatchers orchestrate (L2). NEST view

chunks.title: Repair & field maintenance · NEST
chunks.heading: Indus Towers
chunks.text: Telecom-tower company whose sites are kept running by field technicians How they run their tech Integrated Report 2024-25: a NextGen Tower Operations Centre for real-time monitoring and fast response (uptime above 99.95% reported); remote monitoring and predictive-maintenance technologies as part of digitalising operations end to end. Source: Indus Towers Integrated Report 2024-25 (exchange filing) · checked 11 Oct 2026 What it changes A central operations centre with predictive maintenance means fewer routine site visits and more targeted repairs by field technicians. NEST view

chunks.heading: Start here
chunks.text: Cameras and analytics raise more alerts, and each one still needs a trained person to check it on the ground. Most people enter as security guard, Agniveer, constable recruit. The routes below get you to L1; the ladder underneath shows how the work changes at each rung. NEST view L1 These routes prepare you for L1, Intelligent Proxy . The next rung, L2 Orchestrator , needs time on the job running a crew's work plus several AI tools. NEST view ITI trade ( DGT CTS list ): Fireman , Cyber Security Assistant . chunks.title: NEST · Jobs that stay human, and the verified job fairs that hire for them
chunks.heading: Work with AI, or work for AI.
chunks.text: Some work stays human even as AI spreads. NEST maps those jobs that stay human: physical work plus Human in the Loop roles , where people supervise, correct, approve or take over from AI and robots, and the verified Indian job fairs that hire for them. Work an agent can finish with no human check is out of scope. Pick your side. Work with AI → 17 hands-on domains where AI is a tool: care, building, farming, logistics, safety and more. Work for AI → 5 domains that build and run AI: data centres, chips and robots, power, repair and field data. How roles are evolving: the AI role ladder → four rungs, from L1 Intelligent Proxy to L4 Harness and model builder.

chunks.title: NEST · Jobs that stay human, and the verified job fairs that hire for them
chunks.heading: The AI role ladder
chunks.text: Traditional job roles are evolving with AI. NEST uses a hierarchy of four roles to show how, on both sides: L1 Intelligent Proxy · L2 Orchestrator · L3 Skill developer · L4 Harness and model builder . Each rung builds on the one before, and every domain maps onto them. An Intelligent Proxy works with a second brain of expert skills. The second brain is the AI plus the expert-designed skills the person carries with them; the person using it is the Intelligent Proxy. L1 is the starting rung: someone who uses expert-written AI skills on the job, brings the place, the hands and the judgement, and stays responsible. An idea from NEST Collective (Manoj Sahukar).

chunks.heading: The AI role ladder
chunks.text: L1 Intelligent Proxy Uses expert AI skills; does the physical work L2 Orchestrator Runs several AI tools and a crew's workflow L3 Skill developer Writes the skills others use L4 Harness and model builder Builds the tools skills run on See the AI role ladder →

chunks.title: NEST · Jobs that stay human, and the verified job fairs that hire for them
chunks.heading: Data-centre electrical technician
chunks.text: UPS, switchgear, busbars, generators and power distribution for server halls that run 24×7. Demand signal India's operational data-centre capacity reached 1.6 GW in 2025, with 322.4 MW under construction and more than 8 GW committed and planned (Knight Frank). [1] The sector employs about 86,000–90,000 people; cooling and electrical roles are projected to grow more than 100% through 2029 (Quess). [3] India skill path ITI Electrician (DGT CTS) [18] → apprenticeship at a facility → shift technician. ITI Information & Communication Technology System Maintenance (NSQF 4) for the IT side. [22] Domain: Data centres & cooling → ❄️

chunks.heading: Data-centre cooling / HVAC technician
chunks.text: Chillers, CRAH units, liquid-cooling loops, pumps and leak detection. Demand signal Quess projects cooling and electrical facilities roles to grow more than 100% through 2029. [3] Cushman & Wakefield counts 2,887 MW of upcoming supply by 2030. [2] India skill path ITI Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Technician (2 years) [18] → chiller-plant shift technician → BMS operator. Domain: Data centres & cooling → 🧵

chunks.title: NEST · Jobs that stay human, and the verified job fairs that hire for them
chunks.heading: Fibre & structured-cabling technician
chunks.text: Splicing, testing and labelling fibre and copper inside and between data halls. Demand signal Every new hall in the pipeline above needs cabling crews. [1] India skill path TSSC Optical Fiber Splicer QP TEL/Q6400 (NSQF 3) [24] ; ITI Fiber To Home Technician [18] ; TSSC ICT Technician QP, which names cloud and data-centre equipment. [23] Domain: Data centres & cooling → 🦾

chunks.title: NEST · Jobs that stay human, and the verified job fairs that hire for them

chunks.text: Installing, teaching, calibrating and repairing industrial robots and cobots. Demand signal India installed a record 9,120 industrial robots in 2024 (+7%), sixth in the world; operational stock reached 52,570 units (IFR). [7] India skill path ITI Technician Mechatronics or Industrial Robotics & Digital Manufacturing Technician (2 years each) [18] → OEM service engineer. Domain: Electronics, chips & robotics → 🛩️

chunks.title: NEST · Jobs that stay human, and the verified job fairs that hire for them
chunks.heading: Drone pilot & drone maintainer
chunks.text: Flying survey, spraying and inspection drones; batteries, motors, propellers and repairs. Demand signal 251 DGCA-authorised RPTOs have trained 42,412 remote pilots; 25,791 people were trained in drone job roles under PMKVY by 31 Dec 2025 (PIB, 25 Mar 2026). [8] India skill path ITI Drone Technician (6 months, NSQF 3) [19] or Drone Pilot (Junior) [18] ; DGCA Remote Pilot Certificate through an authorised RPTO. [8] 📍

chunks.text: Standing at the plot, site or asset to capture photos, readings and labels that AI systems learn from. Demand signal AgriStack's Digital Crop Survey app requires the surveyor to be at the field location, [14] and uses geofencing and AI-based image processing to check the data. [15] India skill path No dedicated NSQF qualification found this pass ( TBC ). Surveyors are usually appointed by state revenue / agriculture departments — check your district office. 📡

chunks.text: Fitting, configuring and maintaining meters, sensors and gateways that feed AI and analytics. Demand signal RDSS has sanctioned 20.33 crore smart meters; 4.69 crore were installed under the scheme by 30 Mar 2026. [10] India skill path ITI IoT Technician (Smart City) (1 year, NSQF 3.5) [20] or IoT Technician (Smart Agriculture) [18] ; TSSC Telecom Technician – IoT Devices/Systems QP. [23] 🔋

chunks.text: How roles are evolving

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: The AI role ladder
chunks.text: Traditional job roles are evolving with AI. NEST uses a simple hierarchy of four roles, L1 to L4, to show how: each rung builds on the one before, from using expert-written AI skills on the job to building the tools those skills run on. It applies to both Work with AI and Work for AI .

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: The four rungs
chunks.text: L1 Intelligent Proxy Uses expert AI skills; does the physical work L2 Orchestrator Runs several AI tools and a crew's workflow L3 Skill developer Writes the skills others use L4 Harness and model builder Builds the tools skills run on No rung is a job title or a pay grade, and we give no salaries.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L1 Intelligent Proxy
chunks.text: Uses expert-written AI skills on the job and does the physical work: the most accessible rung today. An Intelligent Proxy works with a second brain of expert skills. The second brain is the AI plus the expert-designed skills the person carries with them; the person using it is the Intelligent Proxy. What you do: Uses the AI tools at hand plus skills written by experts, and does the physical part on site.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L1 Intelligent Proxy
chunks.text: Real examples: Farmers ask Kisan e-Mitra, a voice AI chatbot, in their own language Non-specialist health workers screen patients with AI diagnostic aids Urban Company professionals follow an app that guides diagnosis and SOPs Skills to learn: Clear instructions to an agent; checking an answer against what you see; when to stop and ask a qualified person. Physical-work example: A rural lab instructor loads the rural tech lab skill to plan a safe workshop session, then runs it with the students.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L2 Orchestrator
chunks.text: Runs several AI tools and a crew's workflow, and checks what the agents produce. What you do: Runs several AI agents on one job and reviews what each one produces before anything is used. Real examples: Adani Green's operation centre watches sites across states and suggests corrective action Securitas operators verify alarms before anyone is dispatched Mahindra Logistics' LogiOne puts warehouses and transporters in one view Skills to learn: Splitting a job into tasks; giving each agent the right skill and files; reviewing and correcting output; keeping a record.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L2 Orchestrator
chunks.text: Physical-work example: A fair organiser has one agent draft employer invites, one build the floor plan and one check the safety plan, then reviews all three before the fair.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L3 Skill developer
chunks.text: Turns hard-won experience into tested skills that others load. What you do: Designs and tests skills that let other people's agents do a job the way an expert would. Real examples: Cult Training Academy's certification course for new trainers DGT's Craft Instructor Training Scheme for ITI instructors Garuda Aerospace's drone-pilot course, from theory to simulation to flying Skills to learn: Writing step-by-step instructions, checks and stop-and-ask rules; testing a skill on real cases; versioning and licensing it. Physical-work example: A senior electrician writes and tests a fault-finding skill that junior technicians' agents follow on site.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L4 Harness and model builder
chunks.text: Builds and tests the models and tools that skills run on, with the people who use them. What you do: A domain expert, or an engineer working with one, who builds the AI tools, harnesses, evaluations (evals) or models for their own domain: crop-disease models, lab imaging AI, robot controllers, grid digital twins, data-centre cooling optimisation. Real examples: DeepMind's machine-learning cooling for Google data centres Addverb's own robot software ITC's Krishi Mitra GenAI co-pilot Skills to learn: Programming; how agents call tools; designing evals that measure whether an agent did the job right; how models are trained.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L4 Harness and model builder
chunks.text: Physical-work example: A team builds an eval that checks whether an agent's job-fair safety plan covers every rule in the organiser skill. Expert-designed skills to start from, at any rung: the job-fair organiser skill kit and the rural tech lab skill kit . Read and use them at L1, combine them at L2, use them as models at L3, and test agents against them at L4.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L1 in practice: the Intelligent Proxy
chunks.text: The first rung comes from NEST Collective (Manoj Sahukar): when an expert designs a SKILL, a written set of steps, checks and safety rules that an AI agent follows, every agent that loads it can work like an expert. The person directing that agent does not have to be the expert. They are an Intelligent Proxy : they bring the place, the hands, the judgement and the responsibility, and the skill brings the know-how. NEST is about work that needs a person in a real place, so the proxy is that person, directing agents through skills, a phone browser or the command line while doing the part only a human on the spot can do.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L1 in practice: the Intelligent Proxy
chunks.text: A field technician on a site asks an agent on a phone browser to walk through a fault-finding checklist written by an experienced engineer, then does the physical repair. A farmer asks an agent to read a scheme page, fill the form in the browser and list the papers to carry, then goes to the office with them. A fair organiser loads NEST's job-fair skill and has the agent draft the timeline, employer invites and safety plan, then runs the day on the ground. Vibe coding : someone who is not a programmer asks an agent to do anything that can be done with a command line or a web browser (rename files, build a sheet, make a small web page) and checks the result.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: Start here: L1 next steps
chunks.text: Every route below prepares you for L1, Intelligent Proxy : a certified hands-on skill you can then pair with AI tools on the job. Reaching L2, Orchestrator , usually takes time on the job running a crew's work, then learning to run several AI tools at once. NEST view ITI trades under the DGT Craftsmen Training Scheme : each domain page names the trades that fit it. Apprenticeships under NAPS, through the National Apprenticeship Portal, apprenticeshipindia.gov.in ( PIB, about NAPS ). The National Career Service (NCS) : register, find career centres and job fairs. Sector skill council courses : their qualification packs (QPs) are listed on the National Qualification Register (NQR) .

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: Human in the Loop: jobs that check, correct and take over from AI
chunks.text: As AI takes on routine work, someone still has to check it, sign for it and step in when it fails. Those are Human in the Loop (HITL) roles: people who supervise, correct, approve or take over from AI and robots. Some are at a desk, some in the field, some remote. They cut across Work with AI and Work for AI , and NEST lists them alongside physical work as jobs that stay human.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: Why these roles exist
chunks.text: Accountability Someone has to answer for a decision. Indian guidance keeps that person human. NEST view ICMR's ethical guidelines for AI in healthcare: “Humans should have complete control of the AI based healthcare system and medical decision-making”, with Human in the Loop placing people “in a supervisory role” Kerala High Court policy for district courts, as reported by LiveLaw (19 Jul 2025): human supervision over approved AI tools at all times, and AI not to be used to arrive at findings or orders Edge cases AI handles the common case. The odd one out, such as a borderline post, a strange defect or a stuck robot, goes to a person.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: Why these roles exist
chunks.text: NEST view The Guardian (5 Feb 2026): a content moderator working from a village in Jharkhand classifies images, videos and text that automated systems have flagged Regulation Rules increasingly require a human check on automated systems. NEST view IT Rules 2021, Rule 4(4) (MeitY, updated to 6 Apr 2023): large platforms using automated tools must have “appropriate human oversight”, including a periodic review of those tools Global anchor: EU AI Act, Article 14: high-risk AI must be “effectively overseen by natural persons”, who can override or reverse its output or stop it Liability The firm that deploys AI stays liable, so it keeps people who can override it.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: Why these roles exist
chunks.text: NEST view RBI FREE-AI committee report: “final authority should rest with humans, who should be able to override AI”; regulated entities “remain liable” for autonomous AI; fallbacks include “mandatory human-in-the-loop reviews”

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: Human in the Loop on the L1–L4 ladder
chunks.text: NEST view Our mapping of typical HITL work onto the same four rungs. L1 Intelligent Proxy Reviewer or operator: labels data, checks a queue of AI outputs, flies the drone or takes over the robot, following an expert-written review guide, and escalates what it does not cover. L2 Orchestrator Queue or shift lead: runs several review queues, drones or robots at once, handles the exceptions, and checks reviewers' accuracy. L3 Skill developer Writes the review guidelines, rubrics and escalation rules that L1 reviewers use: the expert skill in the loop.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: Human in the Loop on the L1–L4 ladder
chunks.text: L4 Harness and model builder Builds the evaluation sets, oversight dashboards and override or stop controls, and feeds human corrections back into the model.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: Work for AI: recording skills for robots
chunks.text: Startups in India and abroad now pay workers to record their tasks on first-person (egocentric) cameras, so robots and AI models can learn how a skilled person moves. It is a Work for AI job, and it has its own ladder.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L1 Skilled worker recorded as data
chunks.text: Does their normal task while wearing a head, chest or wrist camera (sometimes motion sensors or gloves), so a robot can learn from their hands and choices. Some work is teleoperation: steering a robot through the task. NEST view Real examples: Workers at a Karur textile factory wore head cameras and smart glasses supplied by Objectways Egolab.AI collects first-person footage from garment workers in Delhi NCR Scroll: Egolab's head-mounted cameras were worn by garment workers at a Pearl Global unit in Gurugram; its company document speaks of “100 million hours of egocentric footage” Micro1 contract workers, including in India, record household chores with head-mounted phones

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L2 Annotator and quality reviewer
chunks.text: Labels actions in the footage (hand poses, grasp points, start and end of each step) and accepts or rejects clips against the brief. NEST view Real examples: Annotators label hand poses, object locations and grasp points frame by frame Micro1 videos are reviewed by AI and a human, then annotated by a human team OkayGo runs consent checks, metadata tagging and multi-layer QC

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L3 Task and capture designer
chunks.text: Writes the task lists, capture protocols and checklists that tell recorders what to do and how, often a senior worker from the trade. NEST view Real examples: EgoData uses standardised capture protocols and task checklists Graveiens AI trains participants on each client's capture protocol

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: L4 Robot and foundation-model trainer
chunks.text: Trains or fine-tunes robot and vision-language-action models on these recordings and tests them on robots. NEST view Real examples: Human Archive is developing ways to fine-tune models on its data and test them on robots Open X-Embodiment pools robot datasets to train generalist RT-X policies Published datasets these roles feed: Ego4D: large egocentric dataset of daily-life activity, filmed in many countries Ego-Exo4D: first- and third-person video of skilled activities such as cooking and bike repair Egocentric-10K: an egocentric dataset collected only in real factories

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: If you are asked to record your work
chunks.text: NEST guidance, not legal advice. NEST view Consent in writing. Know what is recorded (video, audio, motion), who will use it and for what, and how to stop. Bystanders and family members should be asked too. Fair pay, agreed before you start. Ask how time is counted, including set-up and rejected clips. Never pay a fee to join. Data ownership and licence. Ask who owns the recordings, whether they can be resold, and whether your face and voice are removed. Not a surveillance tool. Recordings for robot training should not be used to score or discipline you; ask for this in the agreement. Know the trade-off. These recordings help machines learn your task.

chunks.title: The AI role ladder · NEST
chunks.heading: If you are asked to record your work
chunks.text: Use the work to move up the ladder: reviewing, designing tasks, or maintaining the robots. News coverage of consent and surveillance concerns: Indian Express explainer , Inc42 , Scroll (workers say consent was not obtained; Egolab says it took consent “in our own way”) , MIT Technology Review (1 Apr 2026) .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Start a rural tech lab in your village
chunks.text: A practical guide for NGOs, schools and Gram Panchayats that want a hands-on, multi-skill lab based on the Vigyan Ashram model : the DBRT diploma for youth, or the IBT subject in schools. It covers routes, space, tools, safety, instructors, funding, honest economics and compliance. Every figure links to its source and shows its year. Where we could not confirm something, it carries a To confirm badge with the reason. Pick your route Safety and the law Get the AI agent skill kit

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: About this guide
chunks.text: Vigyan Ashram, at Pabal in Pune district, was started in 1983 by Dr S. S. Kalbag. Its approach, "Rural Development through Education System", rests on four principles: learning while doing, multi-skill training, the school as a production centre (students provide services and the community pays for them), and the instructor as an entrepreneur with demonstrable skills [2] [6] . NEST is independent. This guide describes the Vigyan Ashram model from public documents. It is not written, reviewed or endorsed by Vigyan Ashram or STARS Forum. For current fees, costs, syllabus and training dates, contact Vigyan Ashram or STARS Forum directly : see their sites [5] [15] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: About this guide
chunks.text: To confirm means we found the point in a search summary, a secondary copy or an old document, and could not check it on the official page. The short reason follows the badge. Check it before you rely on it. Back to top

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Safety and the law come first
chunks.text: Read this before any student does paid work Child and adolescent labour. No child (under 14, or the age set by the Right to Education Act) may be employed or permitted to work in any occupation, except helping the family or a family enterprise after school or in vacations, or as an artist. No adolescent (14 to 18) may work in the hazardous occupations and processes in the Schedule: mines, inflammable substances or explosives, and "hazardous processes" as defined in the Factories Act [26] . A 2017 notification expanded the Schedule [27] . The amended Act has no stated exemption for school training.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Safety and the law come first
chunks.text: To confirm How the Act treats paid "production centre" work by students in training is a legal question we cannot settle. Electrical work. Under the CEA safety regulations 2023 (regulation 31), electrical installation work must be done by a State-licensed electrical contractor, supervised by a person with a certificate of competency and carried out by a person holding a State permit, with narrow exceptions such as replacing lamps, fans, fuses, switches and small appliances [28] . Regulation 31(2) adds that work done in breach of this must not be energised or connected to the supply (checked in the gazette text on 12 Oct 2026).

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Safety and the law come first
chunks.text: Paid house wiring for villagers must go through a licensed contractor. Selling food. Food businesses with turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore need FSSAI registration (thresholds in force from 1 Apr 2026) [29] . Register before the lab sells pickles, flour, snacks or any processed food. Child protection. Odisha's 2025 contract for school vocational training partners requires a child-protection policy and POCSO/POSH committees [30] . Adopt the same, even if you never bid for such a contract. Get a labour lawyer's written opinion before students do any paid service work, and before anyone under 18 uses welding, grinding, flammable gas or mains electricity outside supervised practice.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: No paid work for under-14s. Keep paid service orders for adults and older trainees, and keep under-14s to learning tasks. NEST suggestion Write a one-page risk check for each activity (welding, wiring, grinding, food processing, animal handling) before the first session, and post it at the station. NEST suggestion Basics on the wall: first-aid kit and a trained first-aider, a fire extinguisher near welding, eye protection for grinding and welding, RCCB on the lab supply. NEST suggestion Back to top

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: DBRT or IBT: two separate routes
chunks.text: These are two different programmes, not one programme delivered through the other. Pick one, or run both with different learners.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: DBRT: a diploma for youth
chunks.text: The Diploma in Basic Rural Technology is certified by NIOS (National Institute of Open Schooling) [1] [3] . NIOS lists 8th pass as the entry level, 600 hours, and four papers (codes 452 to 455): Our Health, Agriculture & Animal Husbandry, Rural Engineering, and Our Home Environment, each marked 30 theory + 50 practical + 20 internal [3] . At Pabal it is a one-year residential course for ages 16 to 22, followed by an apprenticeship year [1] . The 2024-25 batch had 61 students [10] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: IBT: a subject inside a school
chunks.text: Introduction to Basic Technology is a pre-vocational subject for Classes 8 to 10, taught one day a week (about 10 periods), started in 3 schools in 1987 [6] [13] . It is recognised under NSQF as the Multi-Skill Foundation Course (MSFC) , Levels 1 and 2 [4] [7] , and the Maharashtra SSC board examines it in Class 10 [6] . CBSE also offers a Multi Skill Foundation Course (code 416) [20] . Four areas, both routes.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: IBT: a subject inside a school
chunks.text: In the Vigyan Ashram model, training covers Engineering (fabrication, construction, carpentry, drawing, costing), Energy & Environment (electrical work, motor rewinding, survey, solar, biogas), Home & Health (sewing, food processing, a rural lab), and Agriculture & Animal Husbandry (polyhouse, poultry, goat, dairy, nursery). Computers, design tools and AI tools are now part of DBRT [1] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Three ways a village NGO can start
chunks.text: IBT in a partner school. The school signs up for at least 3 years, sets up the lab and selects instructors to Vigyan Ashram's guidelines; Vigyan Ashram trains and monitors; the board examines Class 10 [4] . This needs a board that recognises IBT/MSFC, or a CBSE school. A DBRT-style course for youth. To award the NIOS diploma you must be, or partner with, a NIOS Accredited Vocational Institution (AVI). For NGOs this includes registration as a society or trust and at least 3 years of existence [25] . Accreditation is applied for online through the NIOS e-Accreditation portal, which lists Vocational Courses (AVI) and trade/course-wise norms [47] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Three ways a village NGO can start
chunks.text: NIOS vocational courses close to a rural tech lab include Basic Rural Technology (452-455), Solar Energy Technician (253), Bio-gas Urja Technician (254), Plumbing and Sanitation (611), Welding and Metal Fabrication (629) and Computer Hardware Assembly and Maintenance (663) [48] . To confirm Current AVI fees and the full eligibility norms sit behind the portal; check them there before you apply. Without accreditation, run an uncertified course, or send learners to an existing DBRT centre (see Who runs it today ). A community lab without a diploma. Run multi-skill sessions and service work, and have learners take an RPL or PMKVY assessment for an NSQF certificate (see Funding routes ).

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Three ways a village NGO can start
chunks.text: NEST suggestion

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Match the route to your learners. School-age children: IBT through the school. Out-of-school youth aged 16 and over: a DBRT-style course. Adults with some skills: the community lab with RPL. NEST suggestion Plan for three years, not one month. IBT is a minimum three-year commitment in the Vigyan Ashram model [4] . A short taster workshop is fine, but budget beyond it. NEST suggestion Back to top

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Plan and partners
chunks.text: School and Panchayat. For IBT, the school provides the rooms, school time, instructors from the community and one maths or science teacher to teach theory and coordinate [4] . A lab committee. The IBT guidelines ask each school to set up a committee: the headmaster, sarpanch, SHG chairperson, an advocate, a press reporter and a community entrepreneur [4] . Training and syllabus. In the Vigyan Ashram model, Vigyan Ashram provides technical support, instructor training, content, and mentoring and monitoring for the life of the project, while the school runs the programme day to day, buys raw material and pays instructors [6] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Plan and partners
chunks.text: STARS Forum (Skills Training for Advancement in Rural Societies), founded in 2010 at Pabal, is a network of NGOs and individuals working on rural vocational skills [15] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Hold one joint meeting first with the NGO board, the Gram Panchayat, the school and interested youth and parents, and write down who provides what. NEST suggestion Ask Vigyan Ashram or STARS Forum for current terms before you budget. The only per-school figures we found are from 2016. NEST suggestion Back to top

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Space, tools and safety by area
chunks.text: Space and utilities. For IBT, Vigyan Ashram asks the school for two classrooms (800 to 1,000 sq ft) , a quarter acre of farm land (can be rented), an electricity connection and a water connection [4] . The NSQF MSFC Level 1 curriculum (Govt of Maharashtra, 2015) gives a "suggestive" tool list and says only basic tools should be bought so that routine tasks can be practised [4] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Space, tools and safety by area
chunks.text: A short starter set from that list: Area Starter tools (from the MSFC list) Safety focus Engineering Hammers, saws, chisels, vice and clamps; steel rule, vernier caliper, spirit level, plumb bob; hand drill; arc welding machine; pipe cutter, bender and wrench [4] Gloves, mask and apron (on the MSFC list) [4] ; eye protection, a fire extinguisher near welding, no under-18s on welding outside supervised practice Energy & environment Multimeter and clamp meter, wire strippers and crimpers, MCB/RCCB, earthing set, non-contact voltage detector, rubber matting, inverter and battery, solar lights; models of a biogas plant and soak pit [4] Training boards, not live house wiring; licensed contractor for paid work [28] Agriculture & animal husbandry Hoes, spades, pruners, grafting and budding knives, soil testing kit, soil auger, shade net, polybags, watering cans, wheelbarrow, weighing balance [4] Protective clothing: apron, mask, gloves, boots (on the MSFC list) [4] ; safe storage of any chemicals Home & health Food-processing utensils, pressure cooker, thermometer, sewing kit [4] Hygiene; FSSAI registration before selling food [29] The published list mixes in items from other trades (refrigeration gear and a foreign electrical code), so trim it to what your services need.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Keep a tool register and an issue log. Vigyan Ashram lists pilferage of tools as an implementation challenge [4] . The skill kit has a template. NEST suggestion Buy for your first service menu, not the whole list: start with the services your village will actually pay for. NEST suggestion Back to top

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Instructors: local artisans, with care
chunks.text: The model. Instructors should be village entrepreneurs with demonstrable skills; local skilled youth are trained as instructors, and a science or maths teacher handles theory [6] . An instructor can run their own business from the school workshop with students helping [13] . The paper bar. The NSQF MSFC curriculum sets the instructor qualification as an ITI certificate, diploma or degree in a relevant field, HSC-vocational, DBRT , or RPL Level 3 or above [4] . An artisan without certificates can qualify through RPL (Recognition of Prior Learning). Training.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Instructors: local artisans, with care
chunks.text: In 2016 Vigyan Ashram's support covered two 6-day programmes at Pabal for 4 instructors per school; instructors without basic technical skills needed a further 1-month course at extra cost [6] . Known problems. Building instructor confidence takes time, and instructors are hard to keep if they are not paid the honorarium they need [4] . As Lend-A-Hand India scaled its version, community instructors were replaced by staff with vocational certificates [20] . Government-funded school courses work differently. Odisha's 2025 contract needs degree- or diploma-qualified vocational trainers aged 18 to 45, budgeted at Rs 20,000 a month each [30] . Artisans fit there as guest lecturers.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Four instructors, at least one a woman. That is what the IBT guidelines ask for [4] . Pair each artisan with a qualified coordinator , pay a fixed honorarium plus a share of service income, and enrol them for RPL so they hold a certificate. NEST suggestion Back to top

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Honest economics
chunks.text: The "school as a production centre" idea is real: students install drip irrigation, rent out knapsack sprayers, make tree guards and poultry cages, build soak pits and test well water [4] . But the published figures do not show service income covering the running costs. These are the only figures we found; each is the source's own, with its year.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Honest economics
chunks.text: Figure Year Source IBT per school: tools about Rs 1 lakh (one-time); instructor honorarium + material about Rs 3 lakh a year; Vigyan Ashram support Rs 50,000 a school 2016 Vigyan Ashram deck [6] Services given by an IBT school: about Rs 40,000 a year (value of services) 2016 Same deck [6] Value of IBT school services: Rs 7,634 (2008-09), Rs 16,929 (2009-10), Rs 26,098 (2010-11) and Rs 24,998 (2011-12) per school on average 2008-12 Annual report 2011-12 [8] Community services by DBRT students at Pabal: Rs 70,000 in the year 2009-10 Annual report 2009-10 [9] Pabal workshop department services Rs 2,01,101 in March; all departments Rs 5,15,050 that month Mar 2024 Status report [11] In the same 2016 deck, services worth about Rs 40,000 a year sit against about Rs 3 lakh a year of recurring cost [6] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Honest economics
chunks.text: "Value of services" is also not profit. We found no independent study of cost recovery. Contact Vigyan Ashram or STARS Forum for current costs. The 2016 figures are a reference point, not today's price. Do not budget from them. Vigyan Ashram: programs for schools · STARS Forum

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Treat service income as a learning tool and a partial offset, not the business model. Fund at least three years from grants. NEST suggestion Keep a price list and an order log from day one, so you can report real income against real costs. NEST suggestion Back to top

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Realistic funding routes
chunks.text: Beware of "NABARD grants for NGOs" posts. NABARD has publicly warned that posts advertising grants for NGOs under its Skill Development & Entrepreneurship among Rural Youth (SDERY) scheme are misleading and that it issued no such announcement. Use only nabard.org or your NABARD Regional Office [34] . Never pay anyone to "process" a grant. Route What it can pay for Who can apply, and the catch CSR (company funds) Schedule VII lists education including employment-enhancing vocational skills, livelihood enhancement, and rural development projects [31] . MCA says the items are to be read liberally [32] . The company decides.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Realistic funding routes
chunks.text: The most realistic route for a new village lab, often paired with a school. VB-G RAM G (replaced MGNREGA) MGNREGA was repealed on 1 Jul 2026 [38] . The new list of works includes training-cum-skill development centres, youth centres, and additional classrooms and laboratories in government schools [39] . Buildings and assets only, planned through the Gram Panchayat plan and approved by the Gram Sabha. Not salaries or tools. PMKVY 4.0 / RPL Short NSQF courses and RPL assessment for learners and artisans. Training providers must be accredited for the job role and on Skill India Digital [36] . To confirm We read a summary of the guidelines, not the PDF. Partner with an accredited centre.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Realistic funding routes
chunks.text: NABARD Skill development and entrepreneurship programmes for rural youth [33] . Two named programmes: MEDP (Micro Enterprise Development Programme), skill and entrepreneurship training for Self Help Group members since March 2006, and LEDP (Livelihood and Enterprise Development Programme), piloted in December 2015 for farm and off-farm livelihoods in clusters, with refresher training, market linkages, handholding and escort support [49] . NABARD also runs Skill Development Programmes, and LEDP can include a grant for demonstration units [50] . Aimed at SHG members and rural clusters, usually through a partner agency.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Realistic funding routes
chunks.text: To confirm nabard.org timed out for us, so programme durations and partner eligibility come from PIB, not NABARD's own pages. Ask the NABARD Regional Office. Samagra Shiksha (school vocational education) Up to Rs 5 lakh per school per job role (one-time) for tools and equipment; up to Rs 5 lakh per spoke school a year to the hub school for trainers, raw material and on-the-job training; up to Rs 3,000 per student a year for transport from spoke to hub schools [46] [35] . Money flows through state-selected training partners. Odisha's 2025 bar: 5 years in skilling, Rs 4 crore average turnover, 1,000 people trained [30] . A new NGO can't bid alone.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Realistic funding routes
chunks.text: Odisha: OSDA / Nua Odisha Placement-linked NSQF training for Odisha youth [37] . For established training partners. To confirm The 2025 eligibility we saw (5 years of operation) came from a copy on an aggregator site. DST SEED TARA: long-term core support for science and technology NGOs as rural field labs, 5 to 15 years [40] . SUNIL: NGO and knowledge-institution projects; Vigyan Ashram with Savitribai Phule Pune University received Rs 93.6 lakh over 2023-25 [41] . TARA needs 10 years of rural technology field experience [40] . SUNIL calls are periodic. A new NGO's route is to partner with an existing grantee.

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Split the ask: building from the Panchayat plan, tools and three years of running costs from CSR, certificates through an accredited PMKVY/RPL centre. NEST suggestion Back to top

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Registrations and compliance
chunks.text: 12A and 80G have new names. From 1 Apr 2026 the Income-tax Act 2025 applies: registration as a Registered Non-Profit Organisation under section 332 (the old 12A/12AB) and approval under section 354 so donors can claim a deduction (the old 80G). Both use Form No. 105 , and orders come in Form No. 107. Regular registration lasts 5 tax years, or 10 if income was at most Rs 5 crore in each of the two previous years [42] . Registrations and approvals granted under the 1961 Act stay valid under the new Act unless they conflict with it (section 536(2)(j)); apply in Form No. 105 at least six months before yours expires [43] . FCRA (foreign money).

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Registrations and compliance
chunks.text: Registration is open to associations operating for at least 3 years; newer ones can seek prior permission for a defined project. All foreign contributions arrive first in the FCRA account at SBI New Delhi Main Branch; at most 20% may go on administration; annual return FC-4; registration lasts 5 years. The 2026 rules print purposes and states on the certificate and require at least Rs 10 lakh of foreign contribution used over two years for renewal [44] . Registration also asks for Rs 15 lakh spent on core activities over three years [45] . To confirm That threshold is from the 2019 FAQ and may have changed. Labour, electrical and food rules: see Safety and the law . Back to top

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Launch checklist and KPIs
chunks.text: Pick the route ( DBRT or IBT ) and the learners. Legal shell: trust, society or Section 8 company; Income-tax registration ( Registrations ). Partners and committee: school, Panchayat, a lab committee [4] ; ask Vigyan Ashram or STARS Forum about training. Asset map: rooms, land, power, water [4] , and the artisans who could teach. Three-year budget from real quotes. Instructor plan: four instructors including a woman [4] , RPL, honorarium. Safety and safeguarding: risk checks, PPE, licensed contractor for paid wiring, FSSAI before selling food, child-protection policy, a labour lawyer's opinion ( Safety ). First service menu with prices and an order log. Measure from day one (below).

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: What to measure
chunks.text: From Samagra Shiksha's vocational KPIs: enrolment (including girls and children with special needs), retention and drop-out, fully equipped labs, practical-to-theory hours, field visits, students passing with a vocational subject, progression to ITI, polytechnic or B.Voc, and placement or apprenticeship [35] . From the Vigyan Ashram model: number and value of community services, Class 10 results, and the share going on to technical courses [6] [8] . Also track: instructor retention, service income against running cost, safety incidents (aim for zero), and enterprises started by alumni within a year. NEST suggestion Back to top

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Who runs it today
chunks.text: Most outcome figures below come from the organisations themselves or from studies they commissioned. The 2022 Springer chapter relies on self-reported surveys and calls for a controlled long-term study [20] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Vigyan Ashram (Pabal)
chunks.text: IBT in "140+ schools in Maharashtra benefiting over 15,000 students" (its 2022-23 report) [7] ; 165 IBT instructors and 50 DBRT students supported in 2023-24 [12] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Lend-A-Hand India
chunks.text: Took IBT to more schools from 2005 and developed it into the MSFC; adopted by more than 600 secondary schools; 331 Maharashtra schools with 18,210 students. Reported results include 56% of MSFC students going on to further vocational education, against 20% of others [20] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: UP "Learning by Doing"
chunks.text: UNICEF, Samagra Shiksha UP, Vigyan Ashram and STARS Forum: from 60 schools in 2021 to labs in 1,772 schools plus 570 PM SHRI schools in 2024-25, with 2,160 teachers trained (their own report) [19] [17] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: STARS Forum
chunks.text: Runs IBT in 15 Maharashtra schools [16] and reports helping spread school vocational training from Maharashtra to states such as Uttar Pradesh [18] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Other DBRT centres
chunks.text: Loksadhana runs IBT and a one-year residential DBRT [21] ; Govardhan Skill Centre (Wada, Palghar) runs a one-year DBRT [22] ; Narmadalaya's VIRT (Madhya Pradesh) runs a two-year DBRT [23] .

chunks.title: Start a rural tech lab: an NGO guide (Vigyan Ashram model) · NEST
chunks.heading: Schools as development centres
chunks.text: BAIF used Ashram schools in Nandurbar as demonstration centres, with expert farmers as demonstrators, in 48 schools from 2009 [24] . An independent overview of IBT is in Azim Premji University's Learning Curve [14] . Related NEST domains: Repair & field maintenance , Energy & utilities , Agri-food , Animal care & veterinary , Teaching & hands-on training . When a batch finishes, organise a job fair . Back to top

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Rural tech lab (India)
chunks.text: You are helping a human set up a safe, honest, hands-on technology lab in a village. You research, plan, draft, and keep checklists and trackers. The human decides and acts on anything involving money, legal commitments, hiring, or minors doing paid work (see "Stop and ask a human" at the end). NEST is independent. This kit describes the Vigyan Ashram model from public documents. It is not written, reviewed or endorsed by Vigyan Ashram or STARS Forum. Never claim it is.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Ground rules (always)
chunks.text: Never invent facts or costs. Every figure must come from the human, a real quote, or a source you can link, with its year. Write To confirm and a short reason when you could not check something on an official page. Current costs come from the source. Tell the human to contact Vigyan Ashram (https://vigyanashram.com/) or STARS Forum (https://starsforum.org/) for current fees, costs, syllabus and training dates. The only per-school figures in this kit are from 2016. Say "Vigyan Ashram model" , not "Vigyan Ashram programme", unless the human has a signed agreement with Vigyan Ashram. Safety and the law first.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Ground rules (always)
chunks.text: Read references/compliance.md and references/space-tools-safety.md before planning any activity. Recommend a labour lawyer's written opinion before students do paid work. Label advice. Tips are NEST suggestions, not rules. Say so. Cite. references/sources.md lists every URL used in this kit.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 1: Intake
chunks.text: Ask: who runs it (NGO, school, Panchayat), its legal form and age, the learners (school students in Classes 8 to 10, out-of-school youth 16+, adults), the village's main livelihoods, the space, power and water available, local artisans, and any money already promised.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 2: Pick the route
chunks.text: Use references/routes-dbrt-ibt.md . DBRT and IBT are separate routes: - IBT in a partner school (Classes 8 to 10, a minimum 3-year commitment). - DBRT-style course for youth (NIOS diploma only through, or with, a NIOS Accredited Vocational Institution). - Community lab without a diploma , with learners certified later through RPL or PMKVY at an accredited centre. Write a one-page route note with the reasons.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 3: Partners and committee
chunks.text: Draft the partner map (school, Gram Panchayat, SHGs, a training partner) and a lab committee charter ( templates/lab-committee-charter.md ). Draft the first enquiry to Vigyan Ashram or STARS Forum. Stop: the human sends it.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 4: Asset map and space
chunks.text: Fill templates/asset-map.csv : rooms (IBT guideline: two classrooms, 800 to 1,000 sq ft), a quarter acre of land, power, water, artisans and their certificates. See references/space-tools-safety.md .

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 5: Tools and safety
chunks.text: Build a first service menu from village demand, then a tool list for it only ( templates/tool-inventory.csv ). Write a risk check per activity ( templates/risk-assessment.md ). No paid house wiring except through a licensed electrical contractor; FSSAI registration before selling food.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 6: Instructors
chunks.text: Use references/instructors-rpl.md and templates/instructor-roster.csv : four instructors with at least one woman (IBT guideline), a qualified coordinator, an honorarium, RPL for uncertified artisans. Stop: the human hires and agrees pay.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 7: Economics and funding
chunks.text: Use references/evidence.md for honest economics and references/funding-routes.md for funders. Build a 3-year budget from real quotes only, and a funding tracker ( templates/funding-tracker.csv ). Warn the human about misleading "NABARD grants for NGOs" posts. Draft proposals. Stop: the human approves budgets, signs and submits.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 8: Registrations and compliance
chunks.text: Use references/compliance.md to list what applies (Income-tax Act 2025 sections 332 and 354 via Form No. 105, FCRA if foreign money, FSSAI, labour, electrical, safeguarding). Stop: the human and their CA or lawyer file.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 9: Safeguarding and consent
chunks.text: Adapt templates/parent-consent-and-safeguarding.md . Under-14s do learning tasks only, never paid work. Adolescents (14 to 18) stay off Schedule processes outside supervised practice. Stop: a lawyer reviews it before use.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 10: Launch and measure
chunks.text: Run the launch checklist in references/routes-dbrt-ibt.md ; set up templates/service-log.csv and templates/kpi-tracker.csv from day one. Report service income against running cost honestly.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Stop and ask a human
chunks.text: Always stop, show your draft, and wait for an explicit "yes" before any of these. A task description is not approval.

chunks.title: Rural Tech Lab skill kit · NEST

chunks.text: Action What you prepare What the human does Money (budgets, purchases, quotes accepted, fees, grant or CSR applications, price lists) budget, quotes to compare, draft proposal approves, signs and pays Legal (registrations, FCRA, tax filings, contracts, MoUs, licences, any statement about the law) checklist and draft text with sources gets a CA's or lawyer's opinion, signs and files Hiring (instructors, coordinators, honorarium, contracts, background checks) role description, roster, draft offer interviews, decides and signs Minors doing paid work (any service order where a student under 18 does work that someone pays for) the activity, its risk check and the legal question gets a labour lawyer's written opinion first; decides Sending or publishing (emails, WhatsApp, letters to officials, posters, social posts) full drafts with recipients reviews and sends Children's data (photos, names, marks, consent forms) a list limited to what consent allows confirms consent and shares If a human has not approved, don't do it and don't route around it.

chunks.text: Report what is ready and what is waiting.
