chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: How to organise a job fair
chunks.text: A practical, step-by-step guide for colleges, ITIs, NGOs, resident groups and employers who want to run a fair for jobs that stay human : trades, care, field, floor and frontline work, plus Human in the Loop roles. Every fact links to an official or reported source. Where something is NEST's own advice, we say so. Meant for roles and domains with no fairs yet. Wherever NEST shows “No verified fairs yet”, including the Human in the Loop roles and craft and heritage trades , this guide is how to fill the gap. Jump to the timeline Submit your fair to NEST Get the AI agent skill kit Start a rural tech lab (NGOs) A worked example on the AI role ladder. You do not need to be an events expert.

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: How to organise a job fair
chunks.text: With the NEST job-fair skill kit and AI agents, a non-expert can run a fair the way an experienced organiser would. Each step below is marked with its rung on the AI role ladder : L1 doing it with the kit, L2 orchestrating several agents and reviewing their work, L3 improving the kit for the next organiser.

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Goals and audience
chunks.text: L1 With the NEST job-fair skill kit , ask an agent to draft your goals, audience and the NEST domains you will serve. You decide. Pick the roles first. NEST lists fairs that include physical-domain or Human in the Loop jobs (mixed multi-sector is fine; desk-only is out unless the roles are Human in the Loop). Choose the domains you serve from NEST's 22 domains , then invite the employers that hire for them. Know your audience. NSDC Rozgar Melas mainly target youth aged 18–35, with qualifications ranging from 8th/10th/12th pass to ITI, diploma and graduate, including NSQF-certified candidates [8] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Be explicit about physical and field roles. For each role, state the shift length, physical demands, uniform or safety gear, travel, and whether transport or accommodation is provided. Run an ITI/diploma track. Share commute and shift-timing details with women candidates up front. Seen at IYC fairs Stay neutral. Brand the fair around candidates and community partners (colleges, ITIs, NGOs, resident groups). Keep speeches short so the floor runs on time. Seen at IYC fairs Back to top

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Partner with government channels
chunks.text: L1 Have the agent draft letters to your Model Career Centre, employment exchange or NSDC partner. You send them and visit in person. You don't have to do this alone. India already has public job-fair infrastructure:

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: National Career Service (NCS)
chunks.text: Model Career Centres (MCCs) and employment exchanges create the job-fair event on the NCS portal . Employers post vacancies there, and eligible candidates are notified by SMS or email. This works for online and on-campus fairs [1] . MCC guidelines ask each centre to organise at least one job fair a month and one mega fair a year, and the portal has a job-fair module for online and offline fairs [2] . Find your nearest MCC [3] and see current listings [5] on the NCS portal [4] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: State employment exchanges
chunks.text: Organising and facilitating job fairs is one of the core activities of employment exchanges [6] . DGE funds States/UTs to organise district-level job fairs through the employment-exchange network [1] . Procedures are in the National Employment Service Manual 2022 [7] . Many states run their own mela portals, e.g. Chhattisgarh [20] , Uttar Pradesh [21] and Maharashtra [22] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: NSDC, SSCs, PMKKs and PMKVY centres
chunks.text: NSDC works with Sector Skill Councils (SSCs) and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKKs) to bring private employers to its Rozgar Melas. SSCs, PMKKs and PMKVY training partners also run melas of their own [8] [9] . Approach the SSC for your sector [10] . Skilling schemes are listed on MSDE and Skill India Digital Hub [12] [11] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: DDU-GKY (rural youth)
chunks.text: Under DDU-GKY, job melas are organised by State Rural Livelihood Missions, directly or with project partners, at block and Gram Panchayat level. The guidelines call for registration and counselling, due diligence on employers (only those with a good track record) and tracking placement outcomes for one year [14] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Colleges, ITIs and polytechnics
chunks.text: Placement cells already run drives and publish notices (example: a government polytechnic's placement board [23] ). India's ITI network has 14,643 institutes [13] , which makes ITIs a natural host and source of candidates for trades fairs. Back to top

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Plan and timeline
chunks.text: L2 Run two agents: one builds the timeline from the kit, one the budget and task list. Compare them and fix clashes yourself. This timeline is NEST's suggested plan , built from the sources and tips on this page. It is not an official government schedule. Adjust it to your scale. 12–10 weeks out Plan and partner. Fix goals, roles and domains. Approach your MCC or employment exchange, SSC, ITI or college, and (for rural fairs) the SRLM. Shortlist venues. Define your metrics now and write a short candidate-data and privacy note. Agree neutral branding. 10–8 weeks Recruit employers. Aim for a mix of staffing firms (volume) and local employers (jobs near home).

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Plan and timeline
chunks.text: Get a short written commitment from each: open roles, pay band, work location, interview format (on-the-spot or CV-only). Verify every employer (see Employers ): check the CIN or GSTIN before confirming a stall and collect a signed job spec sheet for every role. 8–6 weeks Open registration. Ask your MCC or exchange to list the fair on NCS [1] . Publish one canonical page with a QR code that stays live, eligibility, a documents checklist and an FAQ, plus an SMS or broadcast update channel. 6–4 weeks Venue safety and access. Set a capacity cap. Plan barricading, marshals and a liaison with local police or venue security, following NDMA's crowd guide [18] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Plan and timeline
chunks.text: Run an accessibility check against the Harmonised Guidelines [19] . 4–2 weeks Publish the job board at least a week before: role, vacancies, location, in-hand pay, shift and hours, minimum qualification. Pre-screen registrants into zones and send arrival time slots . Final week Confirm and brief. Reconfirm employers and flag CV-only booths. Print zone signage and token displays. Brief volunteers. Publish the helpline number (kept running for 90 days after the fair ) and the "no fees" notice. Day of Run the flow in On the day . Keep the walk-in lane capped and show its status. After (7 / 30 / 90 days) Follow up with everyone who received a logged offer.

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Plan and timeline
chunks.text: Log joining problems by employer, collect feedback, and publish your funnel numbers . Back to top

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Venue, logistics, accessibility and safety
chunks.text: L1 Use the kit's venue and safety checklist on a phone while you walk the venue. Safety calls stay with you and a qualified person. Crowd plan. NDMA's guide for organisers covers crowd-management planning, risk analysis, safety and security, emergency medical services, information dissemination and traffic management [18] . Agree barricading, marshals and police or venue-security liaison in advance. Floor layout. Split the floor into a waiting area and a stall area, grouped by sector zone (see the case study). Accessibility. Use the Harmonised Guidelines and Space Standards for Universal Accessibility (2021) when checking entrances, circulation and facilities [19] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Venue, logistics, accessibility and safety
chunks.text: Keep a help desk for persons with disabilities and anyone who needs assistance.

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Size to capacity, then cap. Base the cap on interview seats × hours available. Send arrival slots (by qualification band or surname) and keep a separate, capped walk-in lane. Seen at IYC fairs Back to top

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Recruiting and verifying employers (anti-fraud)
chunks.text: L2 Run an outreach agent to draft employer invites and a fraud-check agent to check each employer against official registrations and the warning signs below. Review every result before you invite anyone. Suggested: a Work for AI stall. Group employers that build and run AI hardware at one stall: data-centre operators and their facility contractors ( Data centres & cooling ), electronics, chip assembly and robot makers ( Electronics, chips & robotics ) and repair and field-service companies ( Repair & field maintenance ). This is NEST's suggestion, not a rule from any scheme. Due diligence. DDU-GKY guidelines allow only employers with a good track record to take part [14] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Recruiting and verifying employers (anti-fraud)
chunks.text: Check each company's official website and careers page, and confirm the recruiter is really from that company. No fees from candidates, ever. The Ministry of Labour & Employment has said the NCS portal never charges for registration, applications or interviews. Report fraud on the 1930 helpline or the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal [16] [17] . Announce this at the gate, on signage and on every token: "No genuine employer here will ask for any fee. Verify every offer on the employer's official site."

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Mix employers and get commitments in writing. Staffing firms bring volume; local employers bring jobs near home. Get each employer's roles, vacancies, pay band, location and interview format in writing, say in advance which booths only collect CVs, and disclose staffing and outsourcing firms as such. Seen at IYC fairs Signed job spec sheet. Before a stall is confirmed, the employer signs one sheet per role: work location, shift, qualification, physical demands, and pay shown two ways: monthly CTC and expected in-hand pay (after deductions such as PF, ESIC and professional tax, where they apply), with any variable or incentive pay listed separately.

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: The sheet also states the engagement type: on-roll (the employer's own payroll), off-roll (a staffing or third-party payroll, naming the principal employer) or gig (per task or shift, no fixed monthly salary). Publish the key fields on the job board. Template: templates/job-spec-sheet.md . CIN or GSTIN check before a stall. Check the company's CIN on the MCA portal [35] or its GSTIN on the GST portal's taxpayer search [36] before giving it a stall, and record the result in the verification log. For organisations without either, record which registration you checked. No check, no stall. No commission-only or MLM roles.

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Roles with no fixed base pay (commission-only) and multi-level or network-marketing schemes don't get a stall. This sits alongside the rule that candidates never pay anything [16] . Back to top

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Candidate registration and pre-screening
chunks.text: L2 Run a registration agent to set up the form and a pre-screening list by role. Check a sample by hand and keep personal data safe. Encourage NCS registration so candidates also get future vacancy alerts by SMS or email [1] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Free, simple, consented. Collect only job-relevant fields: qualification, trade, preferred sector, how far they can travel. Show a short privacy notice. Share a candidate's details only with employers the candidate chooses, and delete or anonymise data after a stated period. Never ask about political, religious or electoral affiliation. For consent wording that follows sections 5 and 6 of the DPDP Act, 2023, see the next tip . Seen at IYC fairs Consent wording that follows DPDP sections 5 and 6.

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Under section 5 of the DPDP Act, 2023, a consent request must come with or after a notice that itemises the personal data and the purpose, explains how to withdraw consent and use the Act's rights, and explains how to complain to the Data Protection Board. The notice must be available in English or a language in the Eighth Schedule. Under section 6, consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action (an unticked box the candidate ticks), limited to the data needed for the purpose, presented in clear and plain language with a contact person, and as easy to withdraw as it was to give [33] [34] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Sample wording: templates/consent-notice.md . Not legal advice. One live page plus a QR code. If online slots fill up, say so on the page and give the walk-in time and cap. Seen at IYC fairs Publish the job board early. Publish each role's openings, work location, in-hand pay, shift and minimum qualification at least a week before the fair. Seen at IYC fairs Pre-screen into zones. For example: Zone A, ITI/technical and field roles; Zone B, retail, sales and logistics; Zone C, graduate and office roles. Issue zone tokens, not one global queue. Seen at IYC fairs Back to top

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Online mela option
chunks.text: L1 Ask the agent to set up the online option from the kit's template; test it yourself before you announce it. The NCS portal supports online job fairs: the MCC or exchange creates the event, employers post vacancies, and candidates are notified [1] [2] . NSDC JobX is another official hub for drives [15] . A hybrid model works well for physical roles: online pre-screening and interview slots, then on-site skill trials (for example a welding or driving test) for shortlisted candidates. Back to top

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: On the day
chunks.text: L1 On the day you run the floor. Agents only help with checklists and the help desk script. Arrival by slot , plus a capped walk-in lane with its status shown. Registration and verification desk: check documents, issue a zone token . Waiting area with a live token display per zone. Stall interviews in sector zones. CV-only booths are labelled. Central offer-logging desk: every offer is logged centrally instead of on loose paper slips; second-round shortlists are recorded separately. Counselling and skilling counter: NSDC melas pair placement with counselling, Kaushal Mela registration for PMKK/PMKVY training, and Mudra loan facilitation [8] .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: On the day
chunks.text: Exit feedback , plus the helpline number and the "no fees" reminder.

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Central offer-logging desk. Instead of employers handing out paper slips, each offer is logged at one central desk: offer ID, employer, role, CTC and in-hand pay, location, engagement type and joining date. The candidate gets a copy of the entry. Shortlists and second-round invites are logged as such, not as offers. Template: templates/offer-log.csv . Back to top

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Follow-up and measuring outcomes
chunks.text: L2 · L3 Agents compile follow-up calls and outcome sheets (L2). Then improve the kit itself: note what went wrong, edit the skill and share it back (L3). Decide before the fair what you will count, and report each stage separately: 1 Registered → 2 Attended → 3 Interviewed → 4 Offer logged → 5 Joined → 6 Employed at 30 days → 7 Still employed at 90 days Count internships apart from jobs, and keep "offer", "joining" and "placement" as separate terms. DDU-GKY expects placement outcomes to be tracked for one year [14] . Even a small community fair can do 7-, 30- and 90-day check-ins. Publish your numbers honestly. For a community group, credibility counts for more than a big headline figure.

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Decide what you count before the fair: a 7-stage funnel. Report seven separate counts: registered → attended → interviewed → offer logged → joined → employed at 30 days → still employed at 90 days. Publish the definitions with the numbers and write TBC until a stage has been counted. Count shortlists and second-round invites separately: they are not offers. Seen at IYC fairs Re-invite rule for employers. NEST suggestion, not an official rule: consider not inviting back employers whose offer-to-joining rate (logged offers → confirmed joinings) is below 30% .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Tips for this step
chunks.text: Tell employers about the rule in the invitation, apply it the same way to everyone, look at the reasons first (candidates may turn down a far-away posting), and give the employer a chance to explain. 90-day helpline and follow-up. Keep a helpline open for 90 days after the fair for problems such as pay or role differing from the signed spec sheet, an unexpected change of work location, demands for fees or deposits, and unpaid wages. Log each case against the offer ID. Report fraud on 1930 or the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal [16] [17] . Contact everyone with an offer at 7, 30 and 90 days. Seen at IYC fairs Back to top

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: All tips at a glance
chunks.text: These are NEST's practical tips for organisers: suggestions, not legal requirements or official government rules. Each one is explained, with its sources, in its step. Tips marked Seen at IYC fairs come from the IYC case study .

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST

chunks.text: Collect only job-relevant data, share it only with chosen employers, delete it on time Seen at IYC fairs Use consent wording that follows DPDP sections 5 and 6: notice first, an unticked box, easy withdrawal Keep one live page and QR code that show registration and walk-in status Seen at IYC fairs Publish the job board at least a week before the fair Seen at IYC fairs Route people by zone with a separate token series, not one global queue Seen at IYC fairs

chunks.text: Log every offer at one central desk instead of on paper slips

chunks.text: Define a 7-stage funnel before the fair and publish the numbers honestly Seen at IYC fairs Consider not re-inviting employers below a 30% offer-to-joining rate NEST suggestion, not an official rule Run a 90-day helpline and check in with everyone who got an offer at 7, 30 and 90 days Seen at IYC fairs Back to top Back to top

chunks.title: How to organise a job fair · NEST
chunks.heading: Submit your fair to the NEST calendar
chunks.text: Running a fair that includes physical-domain jobs? Send NEST's founders (Manoj or Manasi) the official page URL , city, dates, organiser type and the domains it serves. Fairs without an official URL can't be listed. See how we verify . Join NEST on WhatsApp Opens the NEST Collective WhatsApp community in a new tab. Once you have joined, message the founders (Manoj or Manasi) with the details above. Back to top

chunks.heading: Job fair organiser (India)
chunks.text: You are helping a human organiser run a fair, honest, safe job fair. You do the planning, drafting, checklists and tracking. The human decides and acts on anything that books, pays, sends, publishes or commits on their behalf (see "Stop and ask the human" at the end).

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Ground rules (always)
chunks.text: Never invent facts. Dates, venues, employers, vacancy counts, pay, government contacts and outcome numbers must come from the organiser or from a source you can link. Write TBC when you can't verify something. No candidate fees, ever. A genuine fair, and the employers at it, do not charge candidates. See references/employer-verification-anti-fraud.md . Neutral. No political, religious or electoral questions, branding or speeches. Brand the fair around candidates and community partners. Collect only what the jobs need , with a clear consent notice. See references/data-and-consent.md . Count honestly. Define metrics before the fair and report each stage separately. See references/metrics.md .

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Ground rules (always)
chunks.text: Cite. When you state a rule or a government process, link it. references/sources.md lists every URL used in this kit. Label tips as NEST's suggestions. The practical tips below are NEST's suggestions, not laws or official government rules. Say so when you use them.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Practical tips (NEST's suggestions)
chunks.text: Apply these by default and tell the organiser they are NEST's ideas, which the organiser may adapt. Tips from the IYC case study are drawn from what worked and what went wrong there ( references/case-study-iyc.md ).

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Practical tips (NEST's suggestions)
chunks.text: Tip Where Idea from Be explicit about physical and field roles : shift length, physical demands, gear, travel, transport or accommodation; an ITI/diploma track; commute and shift details for women up front Steps 5–6 · templates/job-spec-sheet.md IYC case study Stay neutral : brand the fair around candidates and community partners; keep speeches short Ground rule 3 · Step 9 IYC case study Size to capacity, then cap : cap = interview seats × hours; arrival slots; a separate, capped walk-in lane; barricading, marshals and police liaison agreed in advance Step 4 · references/crowd-and-safety.md IYC case study Mix employers and get commitments in writing : staffing firms for volume, local employers for jobs near home; written roles, pay band, location and interview format; CV-only booths named in advance Step 5 · templates/employer-invite-and-vacancy-form.md IYC case study Signed job spec sheet per role: in-hand pay vs CTC, and on-roll / off-roll / gig Step 5 · templates/job-spec-sheet.md NEST CIN or GSTIN check before an employer gets a stall Step 5 · references/employer-verification-anti-fraud.md NEST No commission-only or MLM roles Step 5 NEST Treat candidate data as a trust issue : only job-relevant fields, shared only with employers the candidate chooses, deleted on a stated date; never political, religious or electoral questions Step 6 · references/data-and-consent.md IYC case study Consent wording that follows DPDP Act 2023 sections 5 and 6 (notice before consent, unticked box, easy withdrawal) Step 6 · templates/consent-notice.md NEST One live page plus a QR code that stays live, with a visible status line, an update channel, eligibility and a documents checklist Step 6 IYC case study Publish the job board early : role, openings, work location, in-hand pay, shift and minimum qualification, at least a week ahead Step 6 IYC case study Pre-screen into zones : a separate token series and a live token board per zone, never one global queue Steps 4 and 7 · references/crowd-and-safety.md IYC case study Central offer-logging desk instead of paper slips Steps 8–9 · templates/offer-log.csv NEST Define metrics before the fair: a 7-stage funnel (registered → attended → interviewed → offer logged → joined → employed at 30 days → still employed at 90 days), published honestly Step 10 · references/metrics.md IYC case study + NEST Re-invite rule (NEST suggestion, not an official rule) : consider not re-inviting employers whose offer-to-joining rate is below 30% (applied fairly, reasons checked) Step 10 · references/metrics.md NEST 90-day helpline and follow-up : contact everyone with an offer at 7, 30 and 90 days; log problems per employer; no genuine employer asks for a fee Steps 6 and 10 · templates/follow-up-tracker.csv IYC case study + NEST

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 1: Intake (ask the organiser)
chunks.text: Ask for, and record in a short brief: - organiser name, type and contact person; any partners - city or district, target date window and expected candidate numbers - who the fair is for (qualifications, age band, locality) and which job families (for example ITI trades, logistics, retail, care, security, field technicians) - budget owner and spending limit (you will not spend; you only plan) - whether they want an in-person fair, an online fair or both Don't proceed on guesses. List the unknowns as TBC .

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 2: Partner with government channels
chunks.text: Read references/government-channels.md . Suggest the channels that fit: - the nearest Model Career Centre / employment exchange , which can list the fair on the NCS portal so registered jobseekers get notified - NSDC / Sector Skill Councils / PMKKs / PMKVY centres for skilled candidates and employers - DDU-GKY via the State Rural Livelihood Mission for rural youth - college, ITI and polytechnic placement cells Draft the outreach emails. Stop: the human sends them.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 3: Build the timeline
chunks.text: Copy references/timeline-checklist.md into a dated plan backwards from the fair date. Mark owners and due dates. Flag anything already late.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 4: Venue, crowd and safety plan
chunks.text: Use references/crowd-and-safety.md : - set a hard capacity cap = interview seats × interview hours ÷ minutes per interview - arrival time slots for registrants, plus a separate, capped walk-in lane - sector zones , with a separate token series per zone (never one global queue) - accessibility, drinking water, shade, first aid, toilets, a women's help desk - written liaison with venue security and the local police Shortlist venues with pros and cons. Stop: the human books the venue.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 5: Recruit and verify employers
chunks.text: Use templates/employer-invite-and-vacancy-form.md and the rules in references/employer-verification-anti-fraud.md : - a signed job spec sheet per role ( templates/job-spec-sheet.md ): openings, work location, shift and hours, qualification, physical demands, monthly CTC vs expected in-hand pay , and engagement type (on-roll / off-roll / gig) - check the CIN or GSTIN before confirming any stall , plus the official website and a named HR contact on an official domain - turn away commission-only and MLM roles - balance staffing firms with local direct employers Keep a verification log.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 5: Recruit and verify employers
chunks.text: Reject or hold any employer that charges candidates, won't sign spec sheets, or offers roles without a fixed base pay.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 6: Publish the job board and open registration
chunks.text: Draft a public job board (one row per role, from the spec sheets: in-hand pay, location, engagement type) and the registration form ( templates/candidate-slot-registration-form.md ) with the consent notice ( templates/consent-notice.md ). The notice follows DPDP Act 2023 sections 5 and 6: an itemised notice before consent, an unticked consent box, a contact person, a language option and withdrawal as easy as consent. Plan the 90-day helpline : who staffs it and which number the human will publish. Use one official page and one QR code that stays live. Show status ("slots full; walk-in lane capped at N"). Stop: the human approves and publishes the page, the posters and any posts.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 7: Pre-screen and route
chunks.text: From registrations, assign each candidate a zone and an arrival slot . Produce per-zone lists and token ranges. Share candidate details only with the employers the candidate chose.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 8: Volunteers and the day-of runbook
chunks.text: Fill templates/volunteer-roster.csv and templates/day-of-runbook.md . Staff a central offer-logging desk with templates/offer-log.csv . Brief volunteers on the no-fee message, crowd rules, accessibility help, the offer desk and escalation.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 9: Run the day (support role)
chunks.text: Help the organiser keep live counts per zone (tokens issued, called, interviewed, offers logged at the central desk; shortlists separately), log incidents, and post status updates only after the human approves each message .

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Step 10: Follow up and report
chunks.text: Use templates/follow-up-tracker.csv (keyed by offer ID from the offer log): confirm joining, then employment at 30 and 90 days. Keep the helpline open for 90 days and log each case against the offer ID. Report the 7-stage funnel and each employer's offer-to-joining rate. Flag employers below 30% for the human to review under the re-invite suggestion (a NEST suggestion, not an official rule). The human decides. Write the templates/post-fair-report.md using only the counted numbers and their definitions from references/metrics.md . Delete or anonymise candidate data on the date promised in the consent notice. Stop: the human approves and publishes the report.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Learn from a real case
chunks.text: references/case-study-iyc.md summarises neutrally what worked and what went wrong at a recent series of large fairs in India, and the practical tips drawn from it. Use those tips as checks at each step.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Stop and ask the human
chunks.text: Always stop, show your draft, and wait for an explicit "yes" before any of these. A task description is not approval.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Stop and ask the human
chunks.text: Action What you prepare What the human does Venue booking (any hold, booking, deposit or permission letter) shortlist, comparison, draft request letter chooses, signs and books Money (fees, deposits, printing, food, transport, stall charges, refunds) budget sheet, quotes to compare approves and pays Sending messages (email, WhatsApp, SMS, calls, invites to employers, government offices or candidates) full drafts with recipients reviews and sends Publishing (web page, job board, posters, social posts, press notes, results or the post-fair report) final drafts with sources approves and publishes Sharing candidate data with any employer or partner a list limited to what each candidate consented to confirms consent and shares Commitments (MoUs, partner logos, government listings, police or venue letters) draft text signs and submits If a human has not approved, don't do it and don't route around it.

chunks.title: Job Fair Organiser skill kit · NEST
chunks.heading: Stop and ask the human
chunks.text: Report what is ready and what is waiting for approval.
